entries.what_happened: One manuscript, 'The Singer conjecture in dimension four' (OpenAI, dated September 25, 2026; the only manuscript in this family). Its main theorem (thm:main, introduction) says that for any finite connected aspherical integral Poincaré complex Q of formal dimension four, with arbitrary orientation character, the L²-Betti numbers b_p⁽²⁾(Q̃) vanish for every p ≠ 2. Corollary cor:singer-manifolds applies this to closed connected aspherical topological four-manifolds M, which the paper calls the four-dimensional Singer conjecture. The consequences section (cor:euler) adds χ(Q) = b₂⁽²⁾(Q̃) ≥ 0 for the same class, with χ(Q) = 0 exactly when all L²-Betti numbers vanish. For manifolds this is the statement χ(M) ≥ 0 for closed aspherical topological four-manifolds, which is the dimension-four, aspherical case of the Euler-characteristic sign question. The paper also proves χ(M) ≥ |σ(M)| for closed oriented ones (cor:signature) and a growth statement for covers along a descending chain of finite-index normal subgroups with trivial intersection (cor:betti-growth). The main proof is by contradiction. A positive first L²-Betti number yields a nondegenerate continuum boundary with dimension at most one and vanishing Čech H¹ mod 2; the path-pushing section makes it locally connected, and conclusion.tex then contradicts Lemma end:continuum, which says such a continuum has a cut point. The manuscript says nothing about sectional curvature.
entries.delivers: Within the Hopf list, the claim bears only on part (e), Thurston's aspherical sign statement, and only in dimension four. It establishes χ(M) ≥ 0 for every closed connected aspherical topological four-manifold, with no smoothness, orientability or geometric-structure assumption, and more generally χ(Q) ≥ 0 for finite aspherical integral Poincaré complexes of formal dimension four, which need not be manifolds. This is the k = 2 instance of (e), which the list states as (−1)ᵏ χ(M^(2k)) ≥ 0 for closed aspherical manifolds in every even dimension; the manuscript's statement is therefore narrower in dimension and broader in the class of spaces. Parts (a) and (b) (positive and nonnegative sectional curvature) and the curvature-sign parts of (c) are not addressed. Since a closed nonpositively curved manifold is aspherical (Cartan–Hadamard, my note, not the text), the nonpositive case of (c) in dimension four falls under the claim, but the manuscript does not state or prove it, and the problem_asks records dimension four as the already-known case of the curvature conjectures. The product conjecture (d) is not addressed. The manuscript's own statements are not about the list's 'higher-dimensional' scope.
entries.remains: If the claim is correct, the dimension-four aspherical sign statement is settled for closed topological manifolds and for finite Poincaré complexes. Still open for this problem: (a) and (b), the positive and nonnegative curvature sign conjectures in every even dimension; (c), the negative and nonpositive curvature sign conjectures in dimensions 2n ≥ 6; (d), the product conjecture; and (e) for closed aspherical manifolds in dimensions 2k ≥ 6. The paper's Singer-type concentration would give the sign in higher even dimensions only if the vanishing were proved there, and the manuscript proves it only in dimension four.
entries.direction: proves a case: the dimension-four aspherical instance of the Euler-characteristic sign (χ ≥ 0), plus χ ≥ |σ| for oriented topological four-manifolds as a side result; no curvature statement
entries.conditional_on: No hypothesis is assumed for χ(M) ≥ 0 itself. The proof takes cited literature results without reproving them: Wall's dimension theorem and West's homotopy-dimension estimate for the four-dimensional model, topological Poincaré duality (Sun 2017), Bowditch's pretree package, and Lück's L²-Euler–Poincaré formula. It depends on no other OpenAI manuscript for the main theorem. The companion papers are cited only as an application (the PD4 nonmanifold example) and as a remark on complex surfaces, which the text says is not an input. The corollary χ(M) ≥ |σ(M)| additionally needs Lück–Schick's topological L²-signature theorem, and the growth corollary assumes a descending chain of finite-index normal subgroups with trivial intersection. Neither is relevant to the curvature parts of the list.
entries.doubts: (1) The new steps are the authors' own extensions beyond their sources, and the text says so: the finite-interval reduction in the all-parabolic case (pretree.tex: Bowditch's Theorem 6.1 'does not itself produce' it, and 'we now prove that assertion'); the block graph and continuous retraction onto a block (blocks.tex: 'extensions established here, not an invocation of a retraction theorem'); and the separation counts, which the introduction says 'adapt' Bowditch's annulus method. These are the parts a reader must check against the text. (2) The boundary argument runs under standing hypotheses stated at the start of pretree.tex: a finitely presented, torsion-free, one-ended group acting minimally as a convergence group with no nontrivial splitting over a finite or two-ended subgroup. The text says these 'have been established for the boundary constructed above'; I did not check that in foundations.tex or compactification.tex. (3) The four-dimensional model step is compressed. Lemma found:model cites Wall's dimension theorem, justifies finiteness in one sentence ('It can be chosen finite because Q is finite, so its reduced finiteness obstruction vanishes'), and cites West for manifolds. (4) The text presents χ(M) ≥ |σ(M)| as 'the Euler–signature inequality discussed by Gromov and Lück', citing Conjecture 1.3 of Albanese–Di Cerbo–Lombardi, which that source states as a conjecture. The manuscript presents it as a corollary, and says the equality of ordinary and L² signatures is 'an additional input' that is proved only for manifolds. (5) Abstract and main theorem agree: both cover arbitrary orientation characters and both state the manifold case; I found no inconsistency. (6) Reading depth: I read the abstract, introduction, main statements, the conclusion, the consequences, and the openings and flagged passages of foundations, pretree, blocks, annuli and path-pushing. I did not check the full ~3,400 lines of the build, and I did not check the local-connectivity argument in path-pushing beyond its final assembly.
